title: Reconcile interleaved rate-limiter counts from ephemeral namespace proxies
creator: Jordan Alvarez
description: Summary: Several customers reported unexpected 429s and simultaneous token-metering spikes coincident with an internal migration of ephemeral namespace proxy instances. Root cause hypothesis: ephemeral proxy instances were reusing a shared rate-limiter keyspace without properly scoping owner/namespace metadata. When proxy B took over API traffic for proxy A during rolling restarts, counters from both proxies were interleaved in the central rate-limiter store, producing inflated per-tenant counts and causing abrupt throttling and billing anomalies. This ticket tracks investigation, reconciliation, fix, and follow-up hardening to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Deploy two ephemeral namespace proxy pods (proxy-A, proxy-B) pointed to the same logical tenant group with identical owner keys
Simulate steady traffic from client X toward proxy-A until rate-limiter windows are non-zero
Restart proxy-A so proxy-B becomes the active ingress for a subset of connections
Observe central rate-limiter Redis hashes for key collisions and interleaved counters across proxy instance IDs
Trigger extended traffic and compare tenant-specific token counts in billing ledger vs rate-limiter store
telemetry_queries: SELECT namespace, proxy_id, sum(requests) FROM rate_limiter_counters WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '12 hours' GROUP BY namespace, proxy_id ORDER BY sum DESC; -- Grafana/InfluxQL
aws-redshift:SELECT tenant_id, sum(billed_tokens) FROM billing_ledger WHERE day >= '2026-02-01' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 50;
redis-cli --scan --pattern "rate_limiter:*" && for k in $(redis-cli keys 'rate_limiter:*'); do redis-cli HGETALL $k; done  -- inspect cross-tenant fields
acceptance_criteria: 1) Root cause confirmed by repro and telemetry. 2) Code changes deployed that namespace-qualify rate-limiter keys with immutable tenant binding and proxy instance ephemeral suffix avoided. 3) Reconciliation job runs to de-dupe inflated counters and credits affected tenants. 4) Unit + integration tests cover proxy failover paths. 5) No new 429 customer reports for the same class of failover over a 72h observation window.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged fix behind rate_limiter_namespace_flag on staging. 2) Canary to 5% of ephemeral proxies with enhanced logging. 3) Run reconciliation dry-run job to produce a proposed delta ledger and customer-facing credit amounts for review. 4) Schedule maintenance window to apply reconciliation and enable full flag. 5) Monitor SLO dashboards for 72h and run customer notification if any residual billing corrections are required.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Jordan Alvarez: Initial triage: saw customer-reported 429 spikes and matching billing anomalies. Correlated with rolling deploy timestamps. Adding Maya to own the fix and telemetry queries.

2026-02-18 - Maya Chen: Reproduced locally with two proxy pods. Confirmed that the rate-limiter key format was "rate_limiter:<tenant_id>" and proxies were writing HSET fields keyed by proxy-instance-id, which can be re-used across restarts leading to races.

2026-02-20 - Alexei Petrov: Proposed quick mitigation: add immutable tenant binding token to key: "rate_limiter:<tenant_id>:<tenant_binding_id>" and move proxy instance ids to ephemeral subkeys not used for aggregation. Working on tests.
2026-02-24 - Maya Chen: Implemented code changes and local tests. Opened PR 1824. Plan to run reconciliation dry-run to compute what billing deltas would look like for affected tenants.
2026-02-26 - Product (Leah Simmons): Please prepare a customer communication template in case credits are material; we should avoid surprise invoices. Draft ready for review.
2026-02-28 - Maya Chen: Started reconciliation dry-run: found ~12 tenants with inflated counters (median overcount ~3.4%). Preparing a proposed credit ledger and notes for finance review.
2026-03-01 - Jordan Alvarez: Marking In Progress -> adding acceptance criteria and scheduling canary for 2026-03-03. Finance to sign off on credits before full reconciliation.
